direction: User approved Conduit/Overprint synthesis, physical interface idle/dispensing/manual-service states and one architectural build-out. Previous selected qualities inform prompts; new results are not final approval.
scene_invariants: Fixed overhead oblique/trimetric near-parallel camera, continuous floor, five people, four serving trays, principal hall layout. Screen HUD kept separate from world interfaces. Architecture variation documented separately.

studies.title: Synthesis
studies.prompt:
Use case: compositing. Asset: LCL trimetric game style exploration, Round 09 "Synthesis".
Image 1 (Conduit) is the edit target: KEEP its exact scene, five people, four bowl trays, pipe layout, rounded cream-enamel machinery, black ribbed hoses, petrol-blue masonry and floor, coral bands, warm amber pools, bone highlights, dark readable opaque painted treatment. Image 2 (Overprint) is a reference ONLY for actual screen-space HUD. Image 3 (Protocol) is a reference ONLY for the physical circle-over-two-downward-chevrons civic crest.
Primary edit: replace ONLY image1's large ivory screen overlays with Overprint's compact dark charcoal clipped panels, thin bone-white precision rules, assertive typography and sparse coral slash accents. Top-left compact THE LINE / PROVISION card, top-right small SERVICE / MANUAL ACCESS card, bottom four separated small tabs 01 02 03 04 and compact ALLOCATION ACTIVE status at bottom-right; narrow footprint leaving gameplay floor visible. Use brighter white for text and fine key rules, dark for panel bodies, coral for selected04. Screen-space graphics crisp and modular, distinct from opaque painted world. Use the Protocol circle-and-double-chevron crest wherever a civic crest is needed, including HUD; do not import Overprint's broken-ring crest or its physical decals. Keep Conduit's existing physical graphics. Make no additional machine interface hardware yet.
Invariants: exact fixed elevated overhead oblique trimetric near-parallel camera and 16:9 crop of image1, same five people in same positions/poses, same four trays, bench, stairs, columns, shelves, mechanics, palette and illumination. No redesign of machine casing, no broad cleanup of wear. No cinematic horizon, extra characters, floating world labels, added giant panels, imported racing logos, watermark, or title outside the specified HUD. This is the combination control for subsequent physical interface tests.
studies.observations: Five people, four bowl trays, main hall anchors, Conduit rounded housings/hoses, petrol shadows and amber work pools retained. The large ivory cards/strip become dark clipped HUD modules with white rules/text, coral accents and separate 01–04 tabs. Protocol's circle/double-chevron crest stays in the world; the HUD combines it with offset red bars and repeats it on each number tab, a new synthesis detail rather than an exact Overprint copy. HUD wording is legible. Physical bay fascia still only shows 01–03; no new physical console. Fine surface marks shift slightly; fixed camera family and positions remain close, not pixel-identical.

studies.title: Idle
studies.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: LCL Round 09, "Idle". Input1 is the Synthesis edit target.
Add ONE original physical interaction console to the FRONT of the tall cream service tower immediately right of the fourth dispensing aperture and left of the technician. This faces the waiting people, following the tower's world perspective. Put it in the upper half of that tower above the existing coral civic crest; keep that crest visible below. A cast cream protective lip around a recessed dark rectangular readout, one mechanical four-digit counter, a vertical slotted travel indicator, and a large chunky three-detent selector knob are embodied in a single robust panel. This is an actual display and mechanism, not a printed decal and not another screen-space HUD. Module should be readable as a shape/state at the existing game camera, approximately a head wide and a torso high. Bone-white exact "READY" on a dim petrol display, mechanical counter "0004", a thin resting amber indicator at bottom of its vertical slot, selector at its top automatic detent, small upper green readiness lens. Add concise bay identifier "04" on the console bezel. No other new panels or new graphics.
The fourth bay is idle/ready: retain its bowl and tray, dispensing nozzle retracted inside, no flowing contents, static closed cover. All other three bays stay unchanged. Paint the display's diffuse local glow only on its cream lip; it must not relight the hall. Hardware has physical recess, fasteners and service access, crisp white readout subtly subordinated to ambient wear.
Keep the input's exact fixed elevated overhead oblique/trimetric near-parallel camera, 16:9 crop, continuous playable floor, five people with identical positions and poses, four bowl trays, stairs, shelves, benches, palette, opaque painted texture and amber practical lights. Retain compact dark clipped screen HUD, bone-white lettering/rules, coral accents, all existing HUD wording and 01–04 tabs. HUD remains unchanged in every state comparison; state information belongs on the machine itself. Retain the physical circle-over-double-chevron crests and restrained coral collars. No new people, floating labels, exploded diagram, close-up, cinematic horizon, holograms, magical particles, copied brand logos or watermark.
studies.observations: Five people/four trays and screen HUD remain in the Synthesis positions. A world-perspective console is embedded above the service-tower crest, with legible READY, mechanical 0004 counter, green lens, 04 bezel label, narrow orange travel slot and a small top-right selector. The selector is smaller and higher than the proposed chunky lower control, and the slot reads as a lit vertical bar rather than a clear resting marker. Existing bay 04 is identified at the console, not on a matching fascia number. Hardware addition shifts the crest down slightly; tower details and painted microtexture change locally. No flow or extended nozzle visible; primary floor/hall light remains.

studies.title: Dispensing
studies.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: LCL Round 09 "Dispensing". Input1 Idle is the edit target.
Change ONLY the fourth serving bay and its physical console to an active dispensing state. On the existing console above the coral crest, change exact READY to exact "FILL", keep lettering bone-white but make its dim background softly amber; mechanical counter now reads "0003"; move the amber marker in its existing right-side slot to mid-travel, visibly a marker rather than a fully lit bar. Keep rotary selector at automatic position, top readiness lens amber instead of green. In the fourth aperture immediately to the LEFT of this console, show a short metal nozzle descended vertically from its upper cavity toward the existing bowl, a thin visible warm pale food stream into that bowl, and a short amber travel marker built into the tray rail. Keep bowl on the existing tray and tray extended at its current distance. Crisp readable mechanical movement, restrained task light, no spray, steam cloud, decorative effects or magic. Other bays remain static. Counter decreasing is a provisional visual hypothesis, not established lore.
Preserve exact input camera/crop, fixed elevated overhead trimetric near-parallel game view, continuous floor, five people in same poses/positions, four trays, all architecture, material painting, petrol/cream/coral palette and amber practical lighting. Keep all screen-space HUD pixels/design/copy and selected04 tab unchanged. Keep three other bays unchanged. Preserve the new physical console's location, size, casing, bezel04, recessed screen, mechanical counter, right-side vertical slot, top-right rotary knob and civic crest beneath it. This is a state edit of the SAME hardware, not a different interface design. World readouts follow world perspective. No additional floating labels, badges, tooltips, HUD messages, characters, holograms, sparks, cinematic close-up or watermark.
studies.observations: Final corrected image retains five people and four serving trays with exactly one bowl per bay. The fourth bowl sits farther inward under an extended nozzle and visible pale stream; front of its tray is empty. Physical console reads FILL /0003, readiness lens is amber and slot has a compact mid-travel amber marker. Other three bays stay green/static; screen HUD copy/layout retained. Same common console/casing, but rail/nozzle fittings shift locally. The correction softens brushwork and surface detail across the scene somewhat, so medium is close rather than pixel-identical to Idle. Initial draft duplicated the fourth bowl and is excluded from the gallery.

initial_draft.observations: FILL /0003 and amber state readable, extended nozzle/stream and midtravel marker. Accidental two bowls in fourth bay (five total serving bowls), corrected before gallery.

REMOVE the empty bowl at the FRONT tip of this fourth tray. KEEP the bowl at the REAR directly UNDER the extended dispensing nozzle and stream. Leave the exposed front tip as a simple empty dark tray/rail. Final scene has exactly FOUR serving bowls total, one per bay, and four serving trays. The bowl on the fourth tray is temporarily farther inward to receive the portion. Keep the other three bowls untouched. Preserve exactly all five people, their positions, fixed elevated overhead trimetric camera, crop, opaque painting, room, lighting, all machinery/console shape, FILL and0003 readout, amber indicator, flowing portion, crest, dark screen HUD and every HUD word/number. No extra containers or changing other details.
refinements.reason: Remove duplicated fourth-bay bowl while retaining active action.

The lever is a tangible black grip with cream/brass mechanical linkage, plausible human scale. The fourth dispensing aperture immediately left of tower has nozzle retracted and bowl/tray unchanged, no flow. The technician already servicing the neighboring open machine is retained unchanged; do not duplicate or relocate him. Difference should read from knob, open hatch and stopped machine, not just text/colour. Keep the existing larger technician service bay open as it already is.
Preserve exact input camera/crop, fixed elevated overhead trimetric near-parallel game view, continuous floor, five people in same poses/positions, four trays, all architecture, material painting, petrol/cream/coral palette and amber practical lighting. Keep all screen-space HUD pixels/design/copy and selected04 tab unchanged. Keep three other bays unchanged. Preserve the new physical console's location, size, casing, bezel04, recessed screen, mechanical counter, right-side vertical slot, top-right rotary knob and civic crest beneath it. This is a state edit of the SAME hardware, not a different interface design. World readouts follow world perspective. No additional floating labels, badges, tooltips, HUD messages, characters, holograms, sparks, cinematic close-up or watermark.
studies.observations: Same five people/four trays, hall composition, compact HUD and common console location retained. LOCAL and0004 are legible, upper lens amber, and lower tower hatch opens to reveal a brass linkage/lever beneath the retained crest. No flow at fourth bay. Selector pointer/detent change is subtle and not reliably readable at full-scene scale; hatch silhouette is the stronger cue. Right-side slot still appears as an orange lit bar rather than a clearly bottom-resting marker. Some local panel details and surface marks shift; no technician relocation or broader lighting redesign.

studies.title: Service Spine
studies.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: LCL Round 09, "Service Spine". Input1 is the Synthesis edit target.
Explore an architectural build-out of THIS provision hall, keeping the same place and focal machinery. Make the architecture visibly accommodate its system rather than merely shelter it: between the existing rectangular blue masonry piers add a deep dark rectangular service recess following the machine bank; mount ribbed black hoses on an orderly rear cable rack in that recess; a narrow upper maintenance gallery with simple straight brass-dark rails, accessible by the existing left stair; removable rectangular wall access slabs and a floor trench with flush grates in the empty strip immediately behind/under the serving machinery. Use orthogonal civic structural frames and repeating square service portals, contrasting with existing rounded cream machines. A restrained recessed coral strip runs along the service threshold, inset and painted, not neon. Integrate the original existing pipe route with brackets into architecture. Keep human passages wide and bench/shelves usable. Make construction visibly plausible and selective, avoid random pipes. Keep the machine bank shape, four apertures/trays and five people in original positions. Keep the technician and service trolley on the right. Keep most floor open. No new machine interface module; this is the architectural comparison.
Keep the input's exact fixed elevated overhead oblique/trimetric near-parallel camera, 16:9 crop, continuous playable floor, five people with identical positions and poses, four bowl trays, stairs, shelves, benches, palette, opaque painted texture and amber practical lights. Retain compact dark clipped screen HUD, bone-white lettering/rules, coral accents, all existing HUD wording and 01–04 tabs. HUD remains unchanged in every state comparison; state information belongs on the machine itself. Retain the physical circle-over-double-chevron crests and restrained coral collars. No new people, floating labels, exploded diagram, close-up, cinematic horizon, holograms, magical particles, copied brand logos or watermark.
Permitted changes are the architectural wall/recess/gallery/service-depth details behind the machines and the flush service threshold immediately adjacent to them; the main scene layout and camera remain the baseline. Do not transform the hall into a huge industrial exterior or alter human scale.
studies.observations: Five people/four trays and the same compact screen HUD retained with main machine layout and camera. A grated maintenance gallery, rectangular dark rear rack with parallel service conduits/access panels, and continuous front floor trench bordered by coral tile make construction more integrated. The trench ends up in FRONT of the machine, rather than the requested behind/under strip. Extra warm lamps appear on the service wall/gallery and brighten some local background patches; architecture and local lighting therefore vary together. Machine surface marks and lower access panels shift slightly. Main human passage stays open, curved machines contrast with orthogonal service frames; no new physical console.
